t.2.73.1: Then, at daybreak on the fourteenth day, the king-makers assembled and spoke these words to Bharata.
t.2.73.2: Daśaratha, who was our guru, weightier than any other guru, has gone to heaven, having indeed sent into exile Rāma, the eldest, and Lakṣmaṇa of great strength.
t.2.73.3: Become king over us today, O illustrious prince; this kingdom, though without a leader, has not yet fallen away from its concord.
t.2.73.4: O Rāghava, your own people and the guilds have brought all these things for the consecration and are waiting for you, O son of the king.
t.2.73.5: Take up the great kingdom of your fathers and forefathers, O Bharata; have yourself consecrated, and protect us, O bull among men.
t.2.73.7: Kingship has always belonged rightly to the eldest in our family; you, being wise and well-meaning people, ought not to speak to me in this way.
t.2.73.6: Having reverently circumambulated all the articles for the consecration, Bharata, firm in his vow, replied to all those people.
t.2.73.8: For Rāma, our eldest brother, shall be lord of the earth, while I shall dwell in the forest for nine and five years.
t.2.73.9: Let a great army be yoked, mighty in its fourfold strength. I shall bring back from the forest my elder brother, the Rāghava.
t.2.73.10: And placing at the front all this equipment prepared for the consecration, I shall go toward the forest for the sake of Rāma.
t.2.73.11: Having consecrated that tiger among men right there and placed him at the forefront, I shall indeed bring Rāma back, as one brings the sacrificial fire from the sacrifice.
t.2.73.12: I will not let this woman, my own mother in name only, have her desire fulfilled. I myself will dwell in the impassable forest, and Rāma shall be king.
t.2.73.13: Let the road be prepared by craftsmen, both its even and its uneven stretches, and let guards who scout the difficult places follow along on the way.
t.2.73.14: To the king's son, who was speaking thus for Rāma's sake, all the people replied with splendid and unsurpassed words.
t.2.73.15: May Śrī, the lotus-bearing goddess of fortune, attend upon you who speak thus, you who wish to give the earth to the eldest son of the king.
t.2.73.16: O prince, when they heard that matchless speech uttered within their hearing, tears of joy fell toward him, springing from the eyes in the faces of the noble ones.
t.2.73.17: Hearing these words, the ministers together with the assembly rejoiced, their grief dispelled, and said: “At your command, the people devoted to the best of men and the guild of artisans have been assigned to prepare the road.”
